extracted.intended_audience: Mathematica 7 users who create and work with notebooks
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for creating, editing, formatting, and operating Mathematica 7 notebooks: features, keyboard shortcuts, cell/group handling, graphics operations, export, and environment customization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notebook capabilities and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: From simple calculations to full publishable documents and sophisticated dynamic interfaces, everything you can do with Mathematica's standard interactive interface is done in a notebook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notebooks are 'uniquely powerful computational documents' that support 'live computation, arbitrary dynamic interfaces, full typeset input, image input, automatic code annotation, a complete high-level programmatic interface' and use 'thousands of carefully organized functions and options.' Use notebooks when you need interactive, executable, and richly formatted computational documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execute computations (keyboard shortcut)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Shift+Enter to evaluate an input cell. Combine with managing-computation controls (see 'Managing computations') for long-running evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request help or documentation quickly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press F1 on an expression or symbol to access context-sensitive documentation/help within the notebook environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use context-specific menus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Right-clicking in different notebook regions opens menus tailored to the selected object (cells, graphics, text), allowing quick access to relevant operations and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell groups and outlining
rubrics_metrics.description: double-click a group bracket — open or close a cell group; double-click cell brackets — close all other cells in a group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize related cells into groups and use bracket double-clicking for rapid outlining and navigation. Proper grouping makes notebooks easier to read and manage, especially for long documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing computations (interrupt/transfer inputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alt + . — abort a computation; Ctrl + L — copy input from above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Alt+. to abort runaway or long computations. Use Ctrl+L to duplicate or reuse previous inputs when iterating on code or correcting mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and typing helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: triple-click — select a function and its arguments; Subscript (Ctrl+_) ▪ Special Character ▪ Convert to StandardForm ▪ Why the Coloring?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use triple-click to select larger syntactic units (function+args). Use the Subscript shortcut, special-character insertion, and Convert to StandardForm for typesetting and correct input formatting. Be aware of syntax coloring to understand structure and scope while editing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Styling and document structure (cells and styles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alt + 7 — text cell (with default stylesheet); Alt + 4 — section-heading cell (with default stylesheet); Alt + Enter — create a new cell of the same style; Format ► Style ► ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cell styles (text, section headings, etc.) to create structured, readable documents. Alt+Enter to continue in the same style speeds composition. Modify styles via Format ► Style or change the stylesheet for consistent formatting across the notebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylesheet management
rubrics_metrics.description: Stylesheet — (access via Format menu) to control default cell styles and appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose or edit a stylesheet to set the notebook's global visual and structural defaults (fonts, cell spacing, default styles), helpful when preparing publishable documents or sharing notebooks with consistent appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics interaction and drawing tools
rubrics_metrics.description: drag — rotate a 3D graphic; Ctrl + D — open graphics drawing tools (Graphics ► Show Drawing Tools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactively manipulate graphics via mouse drag for 3D rotation; use drawing tools (Ctrl+D) to annotate or create graphics elements. These capabilities support exploratory visualization directly inside notebooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global notebook operations and export
rubrics_metrics.description: Save As ► HTML, etc.; Notebook History; Check Spelling; Send To
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Save As to export notebooks to HTML and other formats for sharing/publishing. Use Notebook History to track changes, Check Spelling for document quality, and Send To to distribute notebooks or content to other applications/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment customization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize the notebook environment (preferences, Option Inspector) to tailor behavior, appearance, and default options to your workflow. Use Option Inspector for fine-grained control of notebook and front-end settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Menu items and insertion tools
rubrics_metrics.description: File ► New ▪ Save ▪ Print ▪ Exit ▪ ...; Insert ► Table/Matrix ▪ Graphics Inspector ▪ Option Inspector ▪ ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with File and Insert menu items for creating new notebooks, saving, printing, inserting tables/matrices, and accessing inspectors. These menu tools streamline common document construction tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further learning and reference (tutorials and help topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tutorials: Notebooks as Mathematica Expressions; Notebooks as Documents. More About: Notebook Shortcuts; Graphics Drawing; Accessibility; International Character Sets; Special Characters; Menu Items
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult linked tutorials and help topics for in-depth explanations and advanced techniques (programmatic notebook manipulation, accessibility, character sets, full shortcut lists). Use these resources to move beyond basics.
